data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.summary: Present perfect continuous for ongoing duration.
sections.explain: Use present perfect continuous to emphasise duration of an ongoing action.

answers.answer: She has been working on the project for three months.
She has worked on the project for three months (emphasis on completion).
She is working on the project for three months.

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.summary: Present perfect for completed results with present relevance.
sections.explain: Use present perfect to focus on the result rather than duration.

answers.answer: She has completed the report, so we can submit it now.
She has been completing the report, so we can submit it now.
She completed the report, so we can submit it now.

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.summary: Past perfect for earlier past actions.
sections.explain: Past perfect is used to show that one past action happened before another.

answers.answer: By the time the meeting started, she had already left.
By the time the meeting started, she already left.
By the time the meeting started, she has already left.

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.summary: Future perfect for completed action before a future time.
sections.explain: Future perfect expresses completion before a specified future point.

answers.answer: By next year, the company will have expanded internationally.
By next year, the company will expand internationally.
By next year, the company will have expand internationally.

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.summary: Present perfect continuous for temporary repeated activity.
sections.explain: Use present perfect continuous to highlight ongoing repeated effort.

answers.answer: Researchers have been studying climate change for decades.
Researchers have studied climate change for decades (less emphasis on process).
Researchers are studying climate change for decades.

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.summary: Past perfect vs past simple sequence.
sections.explain: Past perfect marks the earlier of two past events.

answers.answer: She realised she had made a mistake.
She realised she made a mistake.
She had realised she made a mistake.

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.summary: Present perfect for changes over time.
sections.explain: Present perfect describes changes that continue into the present.

answers.answer: Living standards have improved significantly over the past decade.
Living standards improved significantly over the past decade (finished time).
Living standards have been improved significantly over the past decade.

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.summary: Future perfect continuous for duration before future time.
sections.explain: Future perfect continuous emphasises duration up to a future point.

answers.answer: By 2026, she will have been working here for ten years.
By 2026, she will be working here for ten years.
By 2026, she will have worked here for ten years (no duration emphasis).

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.summary: Present perfect vs past simple with unfinished time period.
sections.explain: Use present perfect when the time period includes the present.

answers.answer: The company has increased its profits this year.
The company increased its profits this year (if year not finished).
The company has been increased its profits this year.

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.summary: Past continuous + past simple for interruption.
sections.explain: Past continuous describes background action interrupted by past simple.

answers.answer: She was presenting when the system failed.
She presented when the system was failing.
She was present when the system failed.
